prompt.name: Ruche mécanisée
prompt.prompt: Create ONE finished 2D/2.5D fighting-game character sprite, ONE full body only, isolated on a truly transparent background. Single static neutral-ready pose facing screen RIGHT, three-quarter side view, head and feet both visible, feet on one common ground baseline. Portrait composition, complete silhouette with at least 5 percent transparent margin all round. Match the refined hand-painted game-sprite style and identity of the first standing figure in the reference, not the whole atlas. Clean solid outlines, precise material shading, readable anatomy and equipment attachments. Do not make a sprite sheet, pose variations, multiple characters, comparison layout, text, captions, UI, backdrop, floor, cast shadow, glow or atmospheric haze. The requested clothes are an original CQC costume, not an official released-game outfit. Preserve the same period-specific character and do not borrow another incarnation. THE PAIN from Metal Gear Solid 3, original costume “Ruche mécanisée”. Preserve his very heavy wide-shouldered operator build and black balaclava identity from the reference. Design a substantial WORN mechanical exoskeleton in weathered mustard-yellow and graphite, with thick hexagonal honeycomb armor panels on chest/shoulders/thighs, dark recessed joints, visibly engineered hydraulic forearm supports, twin compact mechanical reservoir canisters on the upper back. A purpose-designed narrow amber visor sits over his mask; no exposed hair, no organic face shaped robot decoration. His black armored undersuit and heavy boots connect naturally to this frame. Exactly two human legs and two arms, nothing detached, no free-floating insects. The system should feel like a bespoke mobile hive armor, distinct from the pre-existing four-legged robotic Metal Gear version. One relaxed but weighty standing stance facing right.

visualReview.description: Heavy two-legged worn honeycomb exoskeleton, black mask and amber visor; differs from previous quadruped machine variant.
visualReview.limits: Original CQC design; no claim of official outfit or exact recovered historical pixels. Anchor is preliminary and may be refined in catalogue QA.
